title: Google Quantum AI & DeepMind Demonstrate Modular Hyperbolic Codes for Over 30x QEC Overhead Reduction
key_facts: Joint arXiv manuscript by Google Quantum AI, Google DeepMind and MIT researchers
Paper: Low-Overhead Quantum Error Correction with Boundary-Connected Planar Modules
Over 30x lower physical-qubit overhead than standard 2D surface codes
Flat modules of 72 or 116 qubits linked across boundary seams in a hyperbolic tiling
Circuit-level simulations decoded with the AlphaQubit neural network and matching decoders
Tolerates inter-module seam noise of 1%, 10x the on-chip gate error
Fault-tolerant logic via code automorphisms and ribbon extractors about 4.5x smaller than the memory
quote_evidence: Researchers from Google Quantum AI, Google DeepMind, and MIT have introduced a modular quantum error correction (QEC) architecture that reduces physical qubit overhead by more than 30x compared to standard 2D surface codes.

Circuit-level simulations under the SI1000 noise model decoded via the AlphaQubit neural network and correlated minimum-weight perfect matching demonstrated high tolerance to elevated inter-module seam noise.
why_it_matters_hint: Modular chips could ease the wiring problem that has held back efficient qLDPC codes.
